items.title: Warner Bros. CEO Confident Paramount Deal Will Close
items.summary: Warner Bros. Discovery  narrowed its profit in the second quarter, hurt by a large charge, as revenue fell.  The results come as  Paramount  $81 billion deal to buy Warner faces legal challenges by 12 states and the Writers Guild, which seek to block the deal on antitrust grounds.  “We have every expectation the transaction will close,” Warner Chief Executive  David Zaslav  said on a call with analysts Thursday.

items.title: U.K. Waves Through $81 Billion Paramount-Warner Bros. Deal
items.summary: The deal still faces substantial legal challenges in the U.S., where state attorneys general have sued to block the purchase.

items.title: Britain clears $110 billion Paramount-Warner Bros. merger
items.summary: The British government has cleared Paramount Skydance’s $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, saying it had received assurances from the company over media diversity.

items.title: PSKY Beats Q2 Earnings & Revenue Estimates, Reports Strong Q3 Outlook
items.summary: PSKY beats Q2 earnings and revenue estimates as DTC strength, a Studios turnaround and cost discipline offset TV Media weakness, with a solid Q3 outlook.

items.title: Paramount-Warner Bros. merger antitrust trial set for March 2027
items.summary: The March start date means Paramount will owe more than $1 billion in daily penalties before a judge ever rules on the deal

items.title: Paramount Q2 Touts Double-Digit Upfront Gains
items.summary: Paramount Skydance says it had the strongest upfront ad results since the CBS-Viacom merger. The company posted a 9% decline in total ad revenue for Q2, to $1.94 billion.
